This First Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act of 1988 ("the Act") by the Insurance Company aggrieved P.H. Jayani 06 FA505.2018.doc by Judgment and Order dated 09/08/2017, in MACP No. 351/2015 ("the claim"), passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Pune thereby said claim filed under Section 166 of the Act by the Respondent Nos.1 to 4/Original Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Vanita Gajanan Shelke And Ors on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126055761/
1 Claimants has been partly allowed and Respondent No.5/Original Opponent No.1-owner and the Appellant/Original Opponent No.2-insurer held jointly and severally liable pay the Claimants a compensation in the sum of Rs.40,43,527/- along with interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim till realization of the compensation amount.
2) Heard Mr. Mehta, the learned Advocate for the Appellant and Mr. Narvankar, the learned Advocate for Respondent Nos.1 to 3.

3) Mr. Mehta, the learned Advocate for the Appellant, at the outset, submitted that the vehicle in question was duly and validly insured with the Appellant at the time of the accident and the Appellant has no statutory defence against Respondent No.5.
He further submitted that the Appeal is filed mainly on the ground that the compensation amount awarded is exorbitant.
That apart, the claim was proceeded ex-parte against Respondent No.5.
He, therefore, submitted that the notice to Respondent No.5 may be dispensed with.
Mr. Narvankar, the learned Advocate for Respondent Nos.1 to 3 is agreeable to that.
Hence, service of notice to Respondent No.5 is dispensed with, and the Appeal is taken up for final hearing at P.H. Jayani 06 FA505.2018.doc the request of the learned Advocate for the parties.
4) The facts in brief are that Respondent No.1 is widow and Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the daughters and Respondent No.4 was the father of late Gajanan Bhaguji Shelke ("deceased").

The claimants filed the aforesaid claim therein they stated that on dated 12/04/2015, at about 03:15 p.m., on Old Pune-Mumbai highway at Pawana Chowk, Kamshet, within the jurisdiction of Vadgaon Maval Police Station, deceased was crossing the road.
At that time, a motor trailer bearing registration No.MH-46/H-5164 ("the trailer") came there from Pune side.
The trailer was driven in an excessive speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result, the trailer dashed the deceased.
The deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on 13/04/2015 while undergoing medical treatment.

On receiving the report of accident, Vadgaon Police Station registered an FIR No.101/2015 under Sections 279, 337, 338 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act against the driver of the motor trailer.
4.1) The deceased was aged 48 years.
The deceased was working as a Clerk with Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Madhyamik Vidyalaya, Khopoli, Tal. Khalapur, Dist. Raigad and thereby drawing salary of Rs.25,051/- per month.
The claimants were dependent on the income of the deceased.

Therefore,
the Claimants prayed to award P.H. Jayani 06 FA505.2018.doc the compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-
along with interest @ 12 % p.a.
5)
The claim proceeded ex-parte against Respondent No.5.
The Appellant resisted the claim by filing the written statement (Exh.10) therein the Appellant denied that the accident caused due to rash and negligent driving of the trailer.
It was contended that the accident occurred due to fault of the deceased as he was crossing the road without due care.
6) In view of the aforesaid rival pleadings, the Tribunal framed the issues.
On the point of the accident, the evidence of Respondent No.1/PW1 is consistent with the averments made in the claim.

Precisely, her evidence is that the trailer dashed the deceased when the deceased was crossing the Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Vanita Gajanan Shelke And Ors on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126055761/
2 road.

sentences.text: The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the trailer.
The said evidence is corroborated with the Report (Exh.20) on the basis of which the said crime was registered against the driver of the trailer vide Printed FIR (Exh.19).
The Report (Exh.20) was lodged by an eye witness Mr. Nitin Namdev Kedari.
In the report it is clearly narrated that, when the deceased was crossing the road, the trailer came from Pune side and dashed the deceased.

The spot panchanama (Exh.21)
recorded that the road on which the accident occurred, was 24 foot wide.
The road was straight.
The deceased was within the vision of the driver of the trailer.
However, the driver of the trailer failed to avoid accident.
This P.H. Jayani 06 FA505.2018.doc all indicate that the said driver of the trailer did not keep proper look out at the road.
The spot panchnama (Ehx.21) noted that there was 10 feet long tyre mark near the spot of the incident.
Said fact indicates that the trailer was driven at a high speed despite the deceased was crossing the road.
Therefore, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the trailer, is correct.
7) AW2 Dhananjay Chandrasen Mohite (Exh.31) has been working as an Assistant Teacher in the said school.
AW2 deposed that he was doing the work of preparing pay bills of the staff members of the school.
AW1 and AW2 deposed that the deceased was employed in the said school as a Junior Clerk.
To support this evidence, AW2 produced the Service Certificate (Exh.33), Salary Certificate for the period of October 2014 to March 2015 (Exh.34) and copy of the Service Book (Exh.35).
The evidence of AW2 coupled with the Salary Certificate (Exh.34) shows that in the month of March 2015 the salary of the deceased was Rs.25,051/-.
Accordingly, the annual salary income was Rs.3,00,612/-, out of which Rs.2,500/- were payable as professional tax.
Thus, the net annual income of the deceased was Rs.2,98,112/-.
The aforesaid oral and documentary evidence did not receive any challenge in the cross-examination.
Accordingly, I hold that the annual income of the deceased was Rs.2,98,112/-.
The date of birth of the deceased is 06/06/1966, so, he was aged 48 years.
The deceased was in the permanent employment (vide Exh.33).
The Respondent Nos.1 to 3 were dependent on the income of the deceased.
The father of the deceased was aged 75 years and he was also dependent on the income of the deceased.
The father of the deceased expired during pendency of the claim, therefore, his name was deleted.

However, as held in the case of Kirti and others v/s. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.1, "Claims and legal liabilities crystallize at the time of the accident itself and, changes post thereto ought not to ordinarily affect pending proceedings.

sentences.text: Just like how Appellant-claimants cannot rely upon subsequent increases in minimum wages, the Respondent-insurer too cannot seek benefit of the subsequent death of a dependent during the pendency of legal proceedings."

Therefore, in view of the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd.
v/s. Pranay Sethi and Others2 and Sarla Verma and others v/s.

should be added towards her future prospects of the deceased and thereafter 1/4th from the actual net yearly income should be deducted towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased.
The applicable multiplier is '13'.

4, the Respondent No.1 being the widow and Respondent Nos.2 and 3 being unmarried daughters,
are entitled to get Rs.40,000/- each as spousal and parental consortium.
Respondent No.4 late Shri.
Bhaguji Shelke was also entitled to receive Rs.40,000/- as 'filial consortium' but he died during pendency of the claim.

Nevertheless, it cannot be ignored that the remaining claimants are the LRs.
of the father of the deceased.
Therefore, and in view of the decision in Kirti (supra), said filial consortium amount of Rs.40,000/- should be added to the compensation coming to the share of the Respondent Nos.1 to 3.
Additionally, the Claimants are entitled to receive Rs.15,000/- under the head 'funeral expenses' and Rs.15,000/- under the head 'loss to estate'.
The Claimants incurred Rs.38,647/- towards the medical treatment of the deceased before he succumbed to the injuries.
As a result, the Claimants are entitled to get Rs.40,07,227/-.

8) Insofar as the interest part is concerned, the claimants have not produced any evidence to establish that during the relevant period, i.e., from the month of the accident to the date of the decision 4. 2018 ACJ 2782 (SC) P.H. Jayani 06 FA505.2018.doc in the claim, the average rate of interest given by nationalized banks was 9% p.a.
As such, the impugned rate of the interest i.e., 9 % p.a., is certainly on higher side.
Therefore, considering the submissions by Mr. Mehata, the learned Advocate for the Appellant and the facts of the case, I deem it appropriate to award the interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.
Mr. Narvankar, the learned Advocate for the Claimants did not take any exception to that.
9) In the backdrop of the aforesaid discussion, the Appeal partly succeeds.

9.1) Hence, following Order is passed :-
(i) First Appeal is partly allowed with proportionate costs.
(ii) The impugned Judgment and Order dated 09/08/2017, in MACP No. 351/2015 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Pune is modified.
